concept.name: Pipette
concept.definition: One tenth of a pip, i.e. the additional decimal place (the fifth decimal for most pairs, the third for yen pairs) that electronic FX platforms added to quotes. Pipettes allow finer pricing than the traditional four-decimal convention.
concept.intuition: A pipette is the extra digit beyond the pip that lets platforms quote spreads in tenths of a pip.
concept.mechanics: Electronic trading platforms extended quote precision by one decimal place, displaying rates in 1/10-pip increments. In a five-decimal EUR/USD quote such as 1.30105, the last digit (5) counts pipettes; tighter spreads from electronic price competition made this finer granularity necessary.
concept.formula: 1 pipette = 0.1 pip = 0.00001 for most pairs (0.001 for JPY pairs).
concept.failure_modes: Platforms differ in how many decimals they display, so 'points' on one platform may be pips on another; comparing spreads across venues without checking decimal conventions misstates trading costs.
concept.misconceptions: A pipette is not a new minimum tick imposed by any authority — it emerged from platform pricing practice and is not uniformly adopted.
concept.example: If EUR/USD is quoted 1.30105/1.30115, the spread is 1 pipette (0.1 pip), one tenth of the traditional 1-pip minimum increment.
